question: Will Carlos Alcaraz win the 2026 Men's US Open?
resolution_criteria:
The 2026 U.S. Open tennis tournament is scheduled for August 23 - September 13, 2026.

This market will resolve to the player that wins the 2026 U.S. Open Men’s Singles Tournament.

If at any point it becomes impossible for a listed player to win the 2026 U.S. Open Men’s Singles Tournament per the rules of the tournament, the corresponding market will resolve to “No”.

If the 2026 U.S. Open Men’s Singles Tournament is cancelled, postponed after October 31, 2026, or there is otherwise no winner declared within that timeframe, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source will be official information from the U.S. Open (https://www.usopen.org/index.html); however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.
research:
I couldn't open any page directly because the proxy refused every fetch, including usopen.org, ATP, ESPN, Kalshi and Al Jazeera. Everything below comes from search-result snippets. I left out any result dated after 2026-08-26.

## 1. Resolution source
- I couldn't fetch the official source (usopen.org). On 2026-08-26 the tournament is still in its qualifying week. Reports put the main draw at Aug 30 to Sep 13, and no men's singles result exists yet. [ABC/AP](https://abcnews.com/Sports/wireStory/top-ranked-jannik-sinner-withdraws-us-open-knee-135839155)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question. Alcaraz is entered and expected to be one of the top two seeds, and he has not played a main-draw match. I couldn't confirm whether the draw had been made by Aug 26. It usually comes out a few days before the main draw starts.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-23: Greg Rusedski called Alcaraz's return "a huge risk." [Punto de Break](https://www.puntodebreak.com/en/2026/08/23/rusedski-warns-about-alcarazs-return-at-the-us-open-its-huge-risk)
- 2026-08-21: World No. 1 Jannik Sinner withdrew with a right knee injury. He hasn't played since winning Wimbledon in July, he skipped Toronto and Cincinnati, and this is the first major he has missed since 2019. Draper and Rune are also out. [The Star/Reuters](https://www.thestar.com.my/sport/tennis/2026/08/21/tennis-sinner-to-miss-us-open-due-to-knee-injury), [NST](https://www.nst.com.my/amp/sports/racquet-sports/2026/08/1516303/sinner-withdraws-us-open-due-knee-injury-draper-and-rune-also)
- 2026-08-20: Alcaraz confirmed he will return at the US Open after about four months out with a right wrist injury from the Barcelona Open in April. He missed Roland Garros, Wimbledon, Toronto and Cincinnati. [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/8/20/carlos-alcaraz-confirms-us-open-return-after-four-month-injury-layoff)
- About 2026-08-05: He withdrew from Cincinnati, which raised doubts about whether he would defend his title. [Tribune](https://tribune.com.pk/story/2622195/alcaraz-withdraws-from-cincinnati-event-as-doubts-grow-over-us-open-defence), [Hoodline](https://hoodline.com/2026/08/wrist-woes-carlos-alcaraz-quits-cincinnati-new-york-us-open-defense-in-doubt/)
- Undated, probably mid-to-late August: The Daily Beast reported that Alcaraz's Polymarket price dipped after a "rusty" exit from the mixed doubles. I couldn't verify the date or the details. [Daily Beast](https://www.thedailybeast.com/rusty-star-throws-us-open-mens-odds-in-flux/)
- 2026-01: He won the Australian Open, beating Djokovic in the final. That was his 7th major and completed the career Grand Slam. [ATP](https://www.atptour.com/en/news/alcaraz-australian-open-2026-big-titles)

## 4. Base rates
- Alcaraz at the US Open: champion in 2022, semifinal in 2023, second round in 2024, champion in 2025, beating Sinner in the final. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Alcaraz)
- He has won 7 of the last roughly 17 majors he played (2022 US Open through 2026 AO). Since 2024, Sinner and Alcaraz have won almost every major between them. With Sinner out, the main remaining threats are Zverev, Djokovic, Shelton and Fils.
- Against him: no men's US Open champion has defended the title since Federer in 2008. Winning a major straight after a roughly 4.5-month layoff with no warm-up matches is rare in the modern era. I didn't find a systematic statistic on this.

## 5. Other forecasts
- After Sinner withdrew (Aug 21 to 26), sportsbooks priced Alcaraz at about +170 to +240, roughly 29-37% implied. [RG.org](https://rg.org/news/tennis/us-open-mens-odds-predictions-best-bets)
- Oddstrader had Alcaraz +195, Zverev +340 and Djokovic +700. [Oddstrader](https://www.oddstrader.com/betting/mens-us-open-tennis-odds/)
- Kalshi traders priced Alcaraz at about 27-34%. [Kalshi News](https://news.kalshi.com/p/us-open-odds-alcaraz-favored-sinner-withdraws)
- Polymarket had Alcaraz at 26% and Zverev at 22%, from the Daily Beast article; the snapshot date is uncertain. [Daily Beast](https://www.thedailybeast.com/rusty-star-throws-us-open-mens-odds-in-flux/)
- Before Sinner withdrew, Sinner was about -150 and Alcaraz about +185. [Tennisnerd](https://www.tennisnerd.net/news/early-us-open-2026-preview-and-odds-favorites/68136)
- ESPN said Alcaraz is favored but noted he hasn't played since April. [ESPN](https://www.espn.com/tennis/story/_/id/49744097/with-jannik-sinner-carlos-alcaraz-favored-us-open)
- I couldn't load a live Polymarket or Kalshi page dated exactly Aug 26.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- The draw release, probably around Aug 27, will show his path and possible quarterfinal opponents.
- The main draw starts Aug 30. Early rounds will be the first real test of his wrist, serve speed and match fitness. Any flare-up or retirement would end his chances.
- Late withdrawals by other contenders would also matter.
- The question resolves around Sep 9, which is quarterfinal or semifinal time. The final is Sep 13. If he is knocked out before Sep 9, the question resolves No at that point.

Sources: the links above.
